correctness.rationale: The index equals the maximum number of ordered disjoint complete-alphabet blocks: choosing one requested letter from each block proves universality in one direction, while the greedy arch ends followed by a symbol missing from the rest exhibit a missing subsequence in the other. For a palindrome let ℓ be the end of the last of the r greedy arches of its left half, or zero when r=0. An ordered sequence of 2r+1 complete blocks must have its middle block after ℓ (earliest possible end of r complete blocks) and before n+1−ℓ (latest possible start of r complete blocks by reversal). Thus that block must fit in the rest, optional center and reversed rest. At most one block can meet the midpoint, so 2r+2 complete blocks are impossible. The 2r left/right blocks always exist, and one more exists exactly when the odd center is opposite to the nonempty constant rest. This proves the rule including empty or constant halves, rather than assuming the positive-index hypothesis of the cited proposition includes them. Each half-letter then marks two full letters; the two completed-arch types give H=u²y²x⁴[(1−x²)⁻¹+(1−y²x²)⁻¹]. The rest-and-center factors in the frozen proof count all possible centers once with their actual weight and apply u exactly when the midpoint adds a block. Multiplying by (1−H)⁻¹ and clearing the two geometric denominators gives the stated rational identity. I also generated all 1021 palindromes through length 16, encoded their distinct subsequences directly, and checked denominator times the census coefficientwise against the numerator through that length. The length-16 weight-8 example gave counts 2,16,36,16 at indices 2,4,6,8. This is finite corroboration, not the proof. The inspected supplied checker can be replayed with python3 VERIFY.py in the frozen package; it was not executed here.

evidence: Use X=x² and Y=x²y² for half letters. The composition arch formula gives A_0=XY/(1−Y), A_1=XY/(1−X), the terminal-zero and terminal-one parts, and a separate multivariate rest function R. The even piece is E=R/[1−u²(A_0+A_1)].

In the odd palindrome start with x(1+y)E. The palindrome rule marks the completion of the half-rest by the newly appended center with an extra factor u instead of 1. The indexed palindrome proof gives the bijection from successful rests plus their completing center onto complete arches. To count such centers once, not twice, replace its unweighted A(z)/z by A_0/x+A_1/(xy) (one factor removed for the terminal symbol). Thus Φ=[1+x(1+y)]E+(u−1)[A_0/x+A_1/(xy)]/[1−u²(A_0+A_1)]. Clearing denominators gives exactly the frozen numerator and denominator.

In particular the odd-center correction is covered by this implication, not just the even part or the y=1 specialization.
